Horgasm: A Love Story is a super-happy-go-lucky-hilarious-good-time­s rollercoaster that will let you in on the lifestyle of Torstein Horgmo, the record-breaking snowboarder who has become one of the hottest names in the snowboard scene over the last couple of years.

As snowboarding has grown from its small beginnings into a multi-billion dollar industry the scene has changed. See that world through the experiences of Torstein as he travel's the world filming in areas of spectacular scenery or while he competes in Olympic arenas with crowds of thousands. Horgasm: A Love Story goes beneath the surface to show you not only the fun, the friends and the good times, but also the pressures, the highs and lows that have made Torstein who he is. Director Tobias Frøystad has captured an extensive amount of footage and mixed it into one giant entertainment cocktail that will surely inspire and amuse you.

Not sure that you are interested in a snowboarding movie? Don't worry! This is not a movie for snowboarders - rather it's a movie about a lifestyle.

On a personal level, I found this really entertaining to watch, having been someone who's only snowboarded a handful of times. Maybe you'll like it, too!

If I put off roading tires on my city car, will I get better or worse gas mileage?
Worse. more weight, more friction, worse mpg.
Thanks for that. Would I also get worse mpg while off roading vs if I went off roading with city tires?

Depending on the terrain and tires, your value in having the off road tires might pay off more in being off road in the event they help you out of a sticky situation where road worthy tires may be left spinning.

If users do not like the moderator(s) of a sub, those users should move to a new sub. If you really had 2/3rds of the users supporting you, they would all go to the new sub and pretty much kill the previous one anyway.

Allowing users to vote on mods opens the door to brigading. And before you say, "you would need 2/3rds of the subscribers to vote," I will say that when you're asking people to opt into something you're assuming that lurkers will actually do something. But it's easier to do nothing--and what happens if you only get a handful of people to actually vote? Even if you end up requiring a quorum--a minimum number of participants required in order for the vote to count--if that quorum is low you're maybe letting 10 people make the decision for every subscriber. Then you have to decide if non-participants will be counted--and if so, if they will be counted as being for the present mod team or against. So, in addition to being vulnerable to hostile takeovers, it's a messy system that may end up misrepresenting the actual wishes of the subscriber-base.

If YOU like this idea, create a sub and use it there. There's no reason this should be a site-wide policy.

I get why people think this needs to be a thing, and it is not the first time it has been brought up.

My concerns is abuse at that point. A few ways actually. How many subscribers do you need to vote? You will never get them all. So what is stopping a bunch of Anti-GGers from subbing to GG and then ousting the whole mod group?

Second way is more just inconvenience. But crowds are fickle, so a mod makes one bad call so the mod ousts them, even though the mod is really not a bad mod, just made a bad call.

And lastly, if I work super hard to make one of my subs the top sub, could I just be ousted because a bunch of people are just friends with another mod?
